boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations on nearby Near West Side corridors, each with a direct-source reason to stop.

cards.title: Jane Addams Hull-House Museum
cards.subtitle: Halsted Street corridor — 800 S. Halsted St.
cards.notes: Plan a daytime museum stop to see the current exhibitions and programs at this National Historic Landmark beside UIC’s east campus.
cards.short_summary: A free, public historic site focused on social transformation.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum identifies itself as a National Historic Landmark, free and open to the public, at 800 S. Halsted Street.
cards.access_notes: Tuesday–Friday 10:00 a.m.–4:50 p.m.; Saturday 10:00 a.m.–3:00 p.m.; closed Sunday–Monday.

cards.title: National Public Housing Museum
cards.subtitle: Taylor Street corridor — Taylor and Ada
cards.notes: Use the free general-admission galleries to explore housing-history exhibitions; reserve separately only if you want a Historic Apartments tour.
cards.short_summary: A historic house museum and civic cultural center at Taylor and Ada.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum says free general admission needs no reservation and describes its location at the corner of Taylor and Ada Streets.
cards.source_title: Plan your visit to the National Public Housing Museum
cards.access_notes: General galleries are free; Historic Apartment guided tours require a timed ticket. Regular hours are Wednesday–Sunday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m.

cards.title: Scafuri Bakery
cards.subtitle: Taylor Street corridor — 1337 W. Taylor St.
cards.notes: Stop in during bakery hours if you want to browse cookies and pastries rooted in the business’s long-running Little Italy family tradition.
cards.short_summary: A Taylor Street bakery whose family tradition dates to 1904.
cards.evidence_claim: Scafuri Bakery states that it has served the Little Italy community since 1904 and has a Taylor Street location.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current counter hours before going; special orders typically need advance notice.

cards.title: Pompei
cards.subtitle: Taylor Street corridor — 1531 W. Taylor St.
cards.notes: Choose this Taylor Street location for a casual lunch or dinner; the restaurant lists dine-in, carryout, delivery, and drive-up service.
cards.short_summary: A fifth-generation family restaurant with a dedicated Taylor Street location.
cards.evidence_claim: Pompei lists its Taylor location at 1531 W. Taylor Street and says it is open daily for lunch and dinner.
cards.source_title: Pompei — Seasoned with Love for Generations
cards.access_notes: The official site lists the Taylor location as open daily, 10 a.m.–8 p.m.; verify before travel.

cards.title: Al's #1 Italian Beef
cards.subtitle: Taylor Street corridor — 1079 W. Taylor St.
cards.notes: Use the Little Italy counter as a quick meal stop and check the official location page for the day’s service and ordering options.
cards.short_summary: The original Al’s location on Taylor Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Al’s official history says the business reopened at 1079 West Taylor Street in the early 1960s and calls it the original location today.
cards.access_notes: The location page lists Monday–Saturday service and Sunday closure; check current hours before heading over.

cards.entity_name: Shrine of Our Lady of Pompeii
cards.title: Shrine of Our Lady of Pompeii
cards.subtitle: Lexington Street corridor — 1224 W. Lexington St.
cards.notes: Visit respectfully to view a Little Italy religious landmark, then consult the shrine’s schedule before planning around services or events.
cards.short_summary: A Near West Side shrine tied to the area’s Italian-American community.
cards.evidence_claim: The Archdiocese of Chicago lists the Shrine of Our Lady of Pompeii church at 1224 W. Lexington Street.
cards.access_notes: This is an active religious site; check its official calendar or contact the shrine for visitor access.

cards.title: Church of the Holy Family
cards.subtitle: Roosevelt Road corridor — 1080 W. Roosevelt Rd.
cards.notes: Look for public worship or event times before visiting this historic Jesuit church, whose site documents more than 160 years of service.
cards.short_summary: A historic church on Roosevelt Road serving the Saint Ignatius community.
cards.evidence_claim: Church of the Holy Family says it has served Chicago Catholic families for over 160 years and lists its address as 1080 West Roosevelt Road.
cards.access_notes: Public access depends on scheduled worship and events; consult the church calendar before going.

cards.title: Saint Ignatius College Prep
cards.subtitle: Roosevelt Road corridor — 1076 W. Roosevelt Rd.
cards.notes: View the historic school campus from the Roosevelt corridor and use the school’s visitor information if arranging an authorized campus visit.
cards.short_summary: A named Jesuit college-preparatory campus on Roosevelt Road.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Ignatius College Prep identifies itself as a Jesuit Catholic school in Chicago and lists 1076 West Roosevelt Road as its address.
cards.source_title: Saint Ignatius College Prep — Contact Us & Directory
cards.access_notes: This is a school campus; remain in publicly accessible areas unless you have authorized visitor access.

cards.title: Maxwell Street Market
cards.subtitle: Maxwell Street corridor — Halsted Street to Union Avenue
cards.notes: Match a visit to one of the listed seasonal Sunday dates and browse the public market’s vendors, crafts, food, and live entertainment.
cards.short_summary: A free-admission seasonal market in its historic Maxwell Street location.
cards.evidence_claim: Choose Chicago says the 2026 Maxwell Street Market has free admission and runs on Maxwell Street between Halsted Street and Union Avenue.
cards.source_title: Maxwell Street Market: Chicago’s Open-Air Classic
cards.access_notes: The published 2026 dates are May 17, June 7, July 19, August 9, September 13, and October 4, from 10 a.m.–3 p.m.

cards.title: National Museum of Mexican Art
cards.subtitle: 19th Street corridor — 1852 W. 19th St., Pilsen
cards.notes: Take a south-side cultural detour for gallery time; the museum’s visitor page lists free admission and current opening information.
cards.short_summary: A free-admission Mexican art museum in nearby Pilsen.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Museum of Mexican Art says admission is always free and identifies its location in Chicago’s Pilsen neighborhood.
cards.source_title: National Museum of Mexican Art — Plan Your Visit
cards.access_notes: Regular hours are Tuesday–Sunday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; the museum is closed Mondays and major holidays.
